column1: # Path-named flags that auto-approve a sensitive path, with their FACET PROFILE.
# WHY THIS EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM output_flag_worklist.tsv
# That list asks "does this flag write?", which is the legacy band's question. It cannot record WHY
# a row is safe, so its verdicts collapse three different capabilities into one row type — and the
#   --config-file, --conf-path     CONFIGURE · persists by RECONFIGURING future commands. Strictly
#                                  cannot express it — gating these as "write" would record the
#                                  wrong capability and call it closed.
#   --vault-password-file          a SECRET READ on the disclosure axis. Not a write at all; these
#                                  already deny, via a different mechanism.
# So a row here declares what the capability IS. The vocabulary is validated against the engine's
# own enums (src/engine/facet.rs), so an invented or unfilled term is a build error rather than a
#   flag         the flag as spelled in the entry's `valued` list
#   operation    observe | create | mutate | destroy | execute | communicate | configure |
#   locus        process | temp | sandbox-scope | worktree | adjacent | worktree-trusted | user |
#                machine | system-integrity | device | kernel        (`-` only when untriaged)
#   persistence  transient | data | reconfiguring | installing       (`-` only when untriaged)
#   note         the evidence. Required for every triaged row.
# THIS IS A RATCHET, NOT A WORK QUEUE. Do not schedule a campaign against it.
# Measured 2026-08-08: the 787 rows span 285 commands, and 224 of those already carry a
# `researched_version` — i.e. 639 of the rows sit on commands that were ALREADY researched, just
# under the pre-facet standard. Re-researching those commands under the facet taxonomy is the
# existing campaign (see TODO.md), and it is the same work. A second list would compete with that
# campaign for attention while duplicating it.
# So rows leave this file as a SIDE EFFECT of re-research: when a command is redone under facets and
# its path-bearing flags are gated, the row stops auto-approving and the stale check requires its
# deletion. What this file does on its own is FAIL CLOSED on a path-named flag that is not recorded
# — which stops the backlog GROWING while the campaign drains it.
# Its second use is ORDERING, not tracking: a command with rows here has concrete evidence of an
# ungated path capability, which is a reason to re-research it sooner than one that does not.
#   untriaged     seeded 2026-08-08 to hold the line. NOT a safety claim — nobody has looked.
#   not-a-path    the value is not a filesystem location (`--profile` is an AWS/named profile;
#                 `--filename` on some tools is a display label). No capability to profile, so the
#                 facet columns stay `-`, but the note must say what the value IS. Stays forever.
#   in-workspace  the value is a path, but the command binds it inside the workspace by
#                 construction, so it cannot reach a higher rung. Stays, with the binding recorded.
#   pending-gate  a real capability at a rung above worktree, profile recorded, gate NOT yet
#                 applied — normally because the gate needs a mechanism that does not exist yet.
# The population selector is a NAME heuristic (`dir`/`path`/`file`/`folder`), which is deliberately
# dumb. Under-selecting only leaves a flag unswept — never a claim that it is safe — so the selector
# is not a safety boundary and must not be read as one.
# The guard fails in BOTH directions: a candidate missing from this file fails closed, and a row
# that no longer auto-approves fails as stale (it was gated — delete the row).
